protocol.source_text:
Follow-up monitoring of potassium 
 
Sodium Bicarbonate 
Routine use no longer recommended 
Minimal effect on K+ 
May be of benefit in NORMAL ANION GAP METABOLIC ACIDOSIS 
Dosage 8.5% solution 1mEq/kg = 1ml/kg 
Administer in separate IV line to calcium 
CAUSES 
*Impaired excretion 
e.g. renal failure, drugs (spironolactone), 
hypoaldosteronism (Addison’s) 
*Transcellular shifts 
e.g. haemolysis (2 rhabdomyolysis), acidosis, 
hyperglycaemia 
*Measurement error 
e.g. haemolysis during phlebotomy 
CORRECTION FOR ACID-BASE STATUS 
Decrease of pH by 0.1 
= 
Increased K+ of 0.3 – 0.5mmol/l 
e.g. pH 7.1 and K+ 6, then corrected K+ = 5.1 
More useful in mineral met acidosis e.g. renal failure 
than organic acidosis e.g. DKA, lactate 
 
ECG CHANGES 
Peaked T waves 
Prolonged PR interval 
Flattened P waves 
QRS widening 
Sine wave 
Cardiac arrest
